newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Ceval says in talks to sell soy to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Ceval says in talks to sell soy to U.S..

text.p: Brazilian processor Ceval Alimentos said it was in talks to sell 150,000 tonnes soymeal and 230,000 tonnes soybeans to two separate U.S. firms for 15 April-30 May shipment, a company official said.
Ceval said earlier this month it was negotiating to sell soymeal to a U.S. firm but no deal has yet been struck, said Charles Van Der Heyde, director of external trade at Ceval.
"Premiums in Brazil have firmed recently and we are again close to a deal (for soymeal)," he told Reuters. "We are also negotiating here to sell soybeans."
Ceval was offering the soymeal at $300 FOB Brazil and the soybeans at $307 FOB, he said.
"We are negotiating the premium," said Van Der Heyde, adding that the difference between the offer and the demand was around $4.00 for the soymeal and $2.00-3.00 for the soybeans.
The soymeal would be destined for the U.S. East Coast and the beans for the Gulf, he said.
